title: Pre-purchase inspection
subtitle: Based on Mitch's answers and the product labels, checked against NSW requirements. Updated 6 Nov 2026.
source: Termite inspection checklist guide; Inspection Capture (pre-purchase mode); LPC Tech Onboarding Pack (standards, PPE, free service period, never list); Mitch's current pre-purchase inspection agreement (checked 6 Nov 2026); Mitch's answers 6 Nov 2026

sections.heading: The same walk, with a few differences
body: A pre-purchase timber pest inspection is the same physical walk as a regular termite inspection. Use the Termite inspection checklist guide for the steps: interior, roof void, exterior, subfloor and wrap-up. Only the differences are listed here.
The standard is AS 4349.3-2010 for the pest inspection (AS 4349.1 for building). The client is a buyer.

sections.heading: What the law and the label require

items.text: Agreement signed first
items.detail: Do not start the inspection until the Pest Inspection Agreement is signed.

items.text: Roof voids and subfloors: asbestos
items.detail: Houses built before 1990 can have asbestos (roof insulation, eaves, cladding). Do not disturb anything that might be asbestos. Stop and tell Mitch.

items.text: Roof voids: live wiring
items.detail: Look first. Do not touch cables. If you are not sure it is safe, do not go in and tell Mitch.

items.text: Tight or stuffy spaces
items.detail: If you cannot get out easily, or the air feels wrong, do not go in. Tell Mitch first.

items.text: Ladders and heights
items.detail: Work from the ground where you can. Never stand on the top two steps. Keep three points of contact. All four feet down. Tie extension ladders off top and bottom.

sections.heading: What is different
sections.title: In Capture and on site

items.text: Pick Pre-purchase (AS4349.3) as the inspection type in Capture before you start
items.detail: If you start Capture from today's job and the service is pre-purchase, it picks the type for you. Check it before you start.

items.text: The scope is fixed: Pre-Purchase Standard Timber Pest Inspection Report
items.detail: There is no Option 1, 2 or 3 to pick.

items.text: Special conditions or instructions: type in anything the client asked for
items.detail: Leave it blank if there are none.

items.text: Undetected timber pest risk can also be set to Extremely High
items.detail: The choices are Low, Moderate, Moderate-High, High and Extremely High.

items.text: A few findings have different names in Capture
items.detail: Lack of adequate subfloor ventilation. Untreated or non-durable timber used in a hazardous environment. Other conditions conducive to timber pest attack.

items.text: Record any extra tests you used in the Moisture meter and other tests card
items.detail: The pre-purchase report asks whether extra tests were done, and needs the details.

items: You do not fill in a results summary. Mitch builds it from your findings
The report wording says AS 4349.3 where the regular one says AS 3660. Capture does that for you

sections.heading: The client is a buyer
body: The client is the buyer, not the owner. Mitch arranges access. Who is on site varies: it can be the agent, the owner or the buyer.

Mitch sends the Pest Inspection Agreement to the client. Check it has been signed before you go. No inspection results are issued until the agreement is signed and returned. If it is not signed, do not start the inspection. Call Mitch.

sections.heading: Before you go
items: The client has signed the Pest Inspection Agreement Mitch sent

sections.heading: Scope wording
sections.title: From Mitch's current pre-purchase inspection agreement (the one he has used this year). The agreement itself has the full wording.
rows: AS 4349.3-2010, Inspection of buildings, Part 3: Timber pest inspections. AS 3660.2 (termite management in and around existing buildings) is also named in the agreement.
Visible evidence of infestation or damage from subterranean termites, dampwood termites, borers of seasoned timber and wood decay fungi (rot).
Drywood termites and European House Borer are expressly left out. Mould and mildew are not timber pests.

Visual and non-invasive, in areas the inspector decides have reasonable, safe access on the day. No cutting, drilling, dismantling or removing building parts. No disturbing linings or insulation. No moving heavy furniture or stored goods.
The inspector may probe, tap or sound exposed timbers where it is safe. Splinter testing is NOT done when the client is not the property owner, which is the case when the client is a buyer.
Only used where visual signs call for more surface testing.
The inspector cannot inspect inside wall cavities, concealed framing, sealed voids, blocked areas or areas that are unsafe. The report is not a guarantee that the property is free of timber pests.
Roof void: hatch 500 x 400 mm, 600 mm clearance, reachable with a 3.6 m ladder. Subfloor: opening 500 x 400 mm, 400 mm clearance under the bearer, 500 mm beneath a slab. No destructive access.
Strongly discouraged for a pre-purchase. If the client asks for one anyway, it leaves out borers and wood decay fungi and only covers visible termite activity.

sections.heading: PPE
sections.title: From the onboarding pack, when you go in

items.text: Roof void entry: dust mask, gloves, torch, appropriate footwear
Subfloor entry: coveralls, gloves, dust mask, torch
Findings: everything goes in the report
items.detail: If the client asks to talk about what you saw, speak with them.

items.text: The buyer gets the report within 24 hours
Builder at the same time
items.detail: Pre-purchase jobs do not come with a builder. Mitch can organise one for the same time. If the client asks, say so and tell Mitch.

sections.heading: No free service period
sections.body: An inspection has no free service period. It is an inspection only, not a guarantee. The Every job guide has the free service period for treatments.

sections.heading: Job complete when
items: Everything in the wrap-up of the Termite inspection checklist is done
Capture shows Pre-purchase as the inspection type
Special conditions or instructions entered, or left blank because there are none
Any extra tests you used are recorded in the Moisture meter and other tests card
Every inaccessible area and obstruction is recorded in Capture with the specific reason
The client knows the report comes within 24 hours
The job is sent to Mitch from Capture

items.a: Everything goes in the report, and you will have it within 24 hours. Happy to talk it through if you would like.
Mitch will confirm the cost. Mitch will tell you the rough figure to give if a customer asks on site.

items.q: When do I get the report?
Can I get a building inspection done at the same time?
items.a: Mitch can organise a builder to come at the same time. I will pass it on to Mitch.

items.q: Does this mean the house is free of termites?
items.a: It is a visual inspection of the areas we can reach safely on the day. We can't see inside walls or blocked-off areas, so it can't guarantee the property is free of timber pests.

sections.heading: Tell Mitch straight away if
sections.body: Call Mitch on 0432 181 689. After hours or urgent, call Mitch directly.

items.text: You find active termites
items.detail: Do not disturb them. Photograph them thoroughly. Tell Mitch. Termite quotes always go to Mitch.

items.text: You find a major safety hazard
items.detail: Advise the client verbally before you leave site, and tell Mitch. If the buyer is not there, call Mitch straight away and he will tell them.

items.text: The client asks for a quote on anything complex, or you are not sure
items.detail: Say "I'll need to get Mitch to come and have a look and provide a quote for that."

items.text: The client complains or gets aggressive
items.detail: Stay calm and do not argue. For a complaint, tell them Mitch will call them today. If they are aggressive, remove yourself. Call Mitch either way.

items.text: Someone is hurt
items.detail: Treat the injury first. Call Mitch. Write down what happened.

sections.heading: Where this guide comes from
body: Sources: Termite inspection checklist guide; Inspection Capture (pre-purchase mode); LPC Tech Onboarding Pack (standards, PPE, free service period, never list); Mitch's current pre-purchase inspection agreement (checked 6 Nov 2026); Mitch's answers 6 Nov 2026
Safety points checked on 6 Nov 2026 against SafeWork NSW pages. The standards themselves (AS 4349.3, AS 3660.2) are paywalled and were not read.
